paper.title: Generative type-aware mutation for testing SMT solvers

summary.text: Generative Type-Aware Mutation tests SMT solvers by mutating expressions rooted with parametric operators from the SMT-LIB specification, making generation a form of mutation. It is a hybrid of mutation-based and grammar-based fuzzing with an infinite mutation space, which the authors present as overcoming a major limitation of OpFuzz, the previous state of the art for SMT solvers. Their tool TypeFuzz reported over 237 bugs in Z3 and CVC4, 189 confirmed and 176 fixed, including 18 soundness bugs in CVC4's default mode, seven of them two years latent.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Mutation-based testing for solvers rather than DBMSs; SQLancer is cited among the testing work it draws on.
supporting_excerpts: We propose Generative Type-Aware Mutation, an effective approach for testing SMT solvers.

Generative Type-Aware Mutation is a hybrid of mutation-based and grammar-based fuzzing and features an infinite mutation space—overcoming a major limitation of OpFuzz, the state-of-the-art fuzzer for SMT solvers.
During our testing period with TypeFuzz, we reported over 237 bugs in the state-of-the-art SMT solvers Z3 and CVC4.
